## Install R

Download R 4.4 or later from [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org) and run the installer for your platform (Windows, macOS, Linux). This project was built against R 4.5.3. Any recent 4.x release will work.

## Install Positron

Download [Positron](https://positron.posit.co) and install it.

Both Positron and RStudio are built by Posit, but only Positron keeps getting new features. RStudio keeps stability, security and bug-fix updates. Positron is built on the same open-source foundation as VS Code and runs R and Python side by side in one place. For anyone here who already works in Python day to day, the same editor covers both languages.

Once Positron is installed, open it and check it has found your R installation: bottom status bar -> interpreter picker, or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` -> "R: Select Interpreter".

## Get the course materials

Go to the [course repository](https://github.com/franckalbinet/course-mirs-102026) on GitHub, click **Code** -> **Download ZIP**, then unzip it. Open the unzipped folder in Positron (`File` -> `Open Folder…`).

If you already use git day to day, cloning works just as well:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
git clone https://github.com/franckalbinet/course-mirs-102026.git
```

## Install the R packages

This project uses [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) to pin exact package versions, the same idea as Python's venv or conda. It gives you a project-local library instead of your regular R install. `renv.lock` records exactly what's installed. Everyone in the course runs the same versions we tested against.

Open the project in Positron and run, in the R console:

```{.r filename="Console"}
renv::restore()
```

The first run downloads and installs everything listed in `renv.lock` into a project-local library. It can take a few minutes and, on some platforms, needs to compile a couple of packages from source. It touches nothing outside this project folder.

`renv::restore()` can fail behind a restrictive network proxy, on a locked-down institutional laptop, or in similar cases. If it does, install the same packages directly into your regular R library instead:

```{.r filename="Console"}
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "tidymodels", "here", "opusreader2",
  "skimr", "plsmod", "prospectr", "resemble", "hexbin", "glue"
))

install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("mixOmics")
```

This gets you everything you need for the course. It isn't version-pinned. Let us know if something behaves differently from the demo.

## Check everything works

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(here)
library(opusreader2)
library(prospectr)
library(resemble)
library(plsmod)

packageVersion("mixOmics")
```

If that runs without errors, you're set up for the course.
